//: VAZIONIX — FIRESTORE COMPOSITE INDEXES
Every entry below was derived by reading the query that needs it. The file
column is where that query lives; if you delete the query, delete the index.
An index with no query behind it is write amplification nobody is using: it
is charged on every document write, forever, to serve nothing.
SINGLE-FIELD INDEXES ARE NOT LISTED, AND MUST NOT BE.
Firestore creates them automatically for every field, ascending and
descending, and the API REJECTS a composite index that names only one field
('this index is not necessary, configure using single field index controls').
Adding one breaks `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` outright. The
queries in this product that are served by automatic single-field indexes:
users            orderBy usernameLower + startAt/endAt (admin search)
users            where email ==                        (admin search)
users            where referralCode ==                 (signup attribution)
users            where lastSeenAt >= cutoff .count()   (online now)
users            where suspended == true .count()      (admin overview)
users            orderBy createdAt|balance|totalEarned|level desc
(listUsers sorts)
claims           orderBy createdAt desc                (ledger page)
claims           where createdAt >= since orderBy createdAt asc
(earnings chart)
claims           where source == 'challenge'           (challenge state)
notifications    orderBy createdAt desc / where read == false
cooldowns        where kind ==                          (cooldown map)
referrals/list   orderBy joinedAt desc                  (referral table)
tickets          where status == 'Open' .count()         (nav badge)
withdrawals      where status in [...] .count()          (nav badge)
kycRequests|fraudFlags|changeRequests|adRequests  where status == ...
staff            where role == 'super_admin'              (bootstrap guard)
captchaTokens    where expiresAt <= cutoff                (hourly cleanup)
taskSessions     where expiresAt <= cutoff, COLLECTION_GROUP scope — this
one is NOT automatic and is configured in fieldOverrides
below; a collection-group query needs an explicit index
even for a single field.
stats/daily/days orderBy day desc                        (admin charts)
auditLog         orderBy createdAt desc                  (audit page)
messages         orderBy createdAt asc                   (ticket thread)
Comments live in this top-level key, not inside the index objects: the CLI
validates each index against a strict schema and rejects unknown properties.
The order below matches the `indexes` array exactly.
1. entries               board ==, value desc          getLeaderboard() — src/server/social.ts; rankLiveBoard() — functions/src/index.ts
2. entries               board ==, finalRank asc       readRankedBoard() — functions/src/index.ts. Reads a settled period back for the podium snapshot and the prize payout.

3. entries (GROUP)       board ==, value desc          NO LIVE CALLER. The ranking job queries one period path at a time, which the collection-scoped #1 already serves. Kept because the deployment brief asked for the group variant and because a cross-period `collectionGroup('entries')` query is otherwise a rebuild away. Delete it if you never add one — it is charged on every entries write.
4. claims                source ==, createdAt desc     listLedger(source) — src/server/ledger.ts; listRedemptions() — src/server/earn/coupon.ts
5. claims                source ==, day ==             countToday() — src/server/ledger.ts. Every daily cap check in the product.

6. claims                source ==, createdAt asc      shortlinkUsageToday() — src/server/earn/links.ts. An ascending range, which is not the reverse of #4, and it runs on every shortlink page render.

7. withdrawals           uid ==, createdAt desc        listWithdrawals() — src/server/withdraw.ts; getUserDetail() — src/server/admin.ts; and the uid + createdAt >= daily-count aggregate in requestWithdrawal().

8. withdrawals           uid ==, clientRequestId ==    the replay lookup in requestWithdrawal() — src/server/withdraw.ts. Two equality filters, on the money path; an index makes it one seek instead of a merge.
9. withdrawals           status ==, createdAt desc     listWithdrawalQueue() — src/server/admin.ts. Serves both `status ==` and `status in [Pending, HeldForReview, Processing]`.
10. withdrawals           status ==, processedAt desc   getPayoutTicker() — src/server/stats.ts; getFinanceSummary() — src/server/admin.ts.

11. withdrawals           status ==, rail ==, createdAt asc   processDirectWithdrawalBatch() — functions/src/index.ts. Oldest Pending Direct payouts first. `network` is NOT in this index: the job groups by network in memory after the read, so an index with `network` between `rail` and `createdAt` would not serve the query at all.
12. users                 suspended ==, createdAt desc  listUsers({ suspended }) — src/server/admin.ts.
13. users                 suspended ==, suspendedUntil asc   expireSuspensions() — functions/src/index.ts (hourly). Also the read-path repair in liftExpiredSuspension().
14. tickets               uid ==, lastMessageAt desc    listUserTickets() — src/server/support.ts; getUserDetail() — src/server/admin.ts.
15. tickets               status ==, lastMessageAt desc listTickets({ status }) — src/server/admin.ts.
16. ptcAds                enabled ==, tokens desc       listPtcAds() — src/server/earn/links.ts.
17. shortlinks            enabled ==, reward desc       listShortlinks() — src/server/earn/links.ts.
18. challenges            enabled ==, tokens desc       listChallenges() — src/server/earn/daily.ts.
19. offerwallProviders    enabled ==, rating desc       listOfferProviders() — src/server/earn/offerwall.ts.
20. offerwallConversions  uid ==, createdAt desc        listConversions() — src/server/earn/offerwall.ts.
21. lotteryTickets        uid ==, createdAt desc        getLotteryState() — src/server/earn/lottery.ts.
22. lotteryTickets        round ==, status ==           drawLottery() — src/server/earn/lottery.ts and the draw job in functions/src/index.ts. Reads up to 20k Pending tickets for one round.
23. lotteryTickets        uid ==, round ==              the per-round ticket cap aggregate in buyLotteryTickets().

24. taskSessions          kind ==, itemId ==            openTaskSession() — src/server/earn/tasks.ts. Closes an open session before issuing another, which is what stops two tabs completing the same PTC view.

25. chats                 mode ==, lastMessageAt asc    escalateStaleChat() — functions/src/index.ts. Finds AI conversations nobody answered; `resolved` is filtered in memory because a `!=` filter would exclude the documents where the field was never written, which is the normal state of exactly the set this job is looking for.
NOT INDEXED ON PURPOSE, THOUGH IT LOOKS LIKE IT SHOULD BE:
withdrawals  uid ==, status ==   onUserDeleted() runs this pair as two
equality-only queries. Firestore serves equality-only filters by merging
single-field indexes, and the row count per user is a handful. Its own
comment in functions/src/index.ts says the same thing.
FIELD OVERRIDES
taskSessions.expiresAt   ASC at collection AND collection-group scope. The
group scope is what makes a cross-user sweep for abandoned PTC/shortlink
sessions possible at all — without it there is no way to ask 'every
expired session belonging to anyone'.
captchaTokens.expiresAt  ASC only, at collection scope. An override REPLACES
the automatic behaviour, so this deliberately drops the descending index.
This collection takes one write per solved captcha across the whole
platform; halving its index writes is real money, and nothing ever asks
for the newest expiry first.
offerwallConversions.rawPayload  NOT indexed. It is the provider's raw
payload: an arbitrary map whose keys we do not control. Firestore indexes
every leaf of a map, so an unbounded key set means unbounded index
entries, and a large payload can breach the 7.5 KiB index-entry limit and
make the write FAIL. Never queried; retained for dispute resolution.
claims.meta              NOT indexed. Same argument, on the hottest
collection in the product.
adUnits.html             NOT indexed. Ad snippets are multi-kilobyte and
an indexed string that size can breach the same limit and reject the save,
which would present as 'the admin console will not let me paste my tag'.
messages.body            NOT indexed. Ticket and chat bodies: free text,
never filtered on, and the collection group is shared by both.
TTL POLICIES ARE NOT DECLARED HERE, ON PURPOSE. `captchaTokens.expiresAt` and
`taskSessions.expiresAt` both want a Firestore TTL policy. Whether the CLI
accepts a `ttl` flag in a field override depends on its version, and an
unknown property fails the entire deploy — so the policies are created out of
band. DEPLOY.md has the gcloud commands and the console path.
